title: A batch runner's standing duty is a rolling combine train, written into decision session-tiers and the project-ops batch-runner template
why: Owner 21:48 CST Nov 13, in runner 10's chat (relayed by the consultant): the combining should be continuous, with lane PRs always joining a batch, so the runner becomes a scaling machine; if sound, make it part of how a batch runner is briefed and operates.
source: Consultant 21:49 CST Nov 13, relaying runner 10 relaying the owner; retrospective agrees.
note: Triage 21:49 CST Nov 13: duty as the consultant states it: a batch closes when its real PR is built and linted, later hand-ins join the next batch, clashing members leave by name. Each merge report carries per-batch numbers: members in, members left out, clash rate, dry-round minutes, lint minutes and CI minutes. Review after 3 batches against lone merges: does the train save time. Homes: decision session-tiers (batch runner) and the project-ops batch-runner template, via a lane the coordinator assigns; a fresh reviewer reads it, since it changes a role's duty. Rule: no rule or guard changes here; merges stay serial. Unmeasured by triage: whether a train beats lone merges; the review is how that gets measured.
